prompt.context: Fire Proof Inc. is a manufacturing company that signs contracts with municipalities and cities to supply fire proof apparel and equipment to fire departments nationwide. The company currently sells fire resistant jackets, gloves, hard-hats, and tools exclusively to government-sponsored fire departments. Fire Proof does $500M in annual sales and has been growing at 4% per year over the last 5 years. They are the number one player in the fire equipment market, but face 3 main competitors who compete for government contracts. Those competitors are more diversified — fire equipment makes up no more than 25% of each competitor's revenue. Fire Proof has historically focused on mastering its core operations rather than diversifying.
prompt.question: The CEO of Fire Proof Inc. wants to find new ways to diversify her revenue and product line. The CEO believes the company can expand their operations to make equipment for other industries. How would you advise Fire Proof Inc.?

clarifying_info.q: How does Fire Proof Inc. make money?
clarifying_info.a: They sign contracts with municipalities and cities to supply fire proof apparel to fire departments.

clarifying_info.q: How large is Fire Proof Inc.?
clarifying_info.a: Fire Proof Inc. does $500M in annual sales and has been growing at 4% yearly over the last 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: What is Fire Proof's market position and how many competitors do they have?
clarifying_info.a: Fire Proof is number 1 in the fire equipment market but they have 3 main competitors that compete for government contracts.
Fire equipment makes up no more than 25% of all 3 competitors' revenue.

clarifying_info.q: Why hasn't Fire Proof diversified before?
clarifying_info.a: The company focused on mastering what they knew and improving their operations in building fire equipment.

exhibits.title: Police Equipment — Market Data
exhibits.shows: A table comparing seven police equipment product categories across four dimensions: Production Overlap, Market Size, Market Growth (annual over last 3 years), and Number of Competitors.

framework: Internal Capabilities: manufacturing capacity (can we build it?), supply chain capacity (do we have the network?), industry knowledge (do they have the talent?), financial resources (can Fire Proof afford the required investment?)

Product Similarities: raw material overlap (can we use the same materials?), customer overlap (are the customers similar — e.g., government?), production overlap (is the manufacturing process similar?)
Market Attractiveness: number of competitors in the new industry, size of the new market, whether the new market is growing, barriers to entry
Financials: investment required to enter the new market, acquire vs. build internally decision, new profit margins achievable, break-even timeline

questions.prompt: Which product market is the most attractive and which is the least attractive for Fire Proof to enter, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidates should evaluate each product against four criteria — production overlap, market size, market growth, and number of competitors (higher = more fragmented = easier entry). Most attractive: Bullet Proof Vests — high production overlap, second-largest market ($600M), double-digit growth (10%), fragmented market (20 competitors). Least attractive: Police Badges — low production overlap, smallest market ($100M), low growth (3%), concentrated market (4 competitors). Bonus observations: Officer Uniforms are interesting for size and overlap but the concentrated market (3 competitors) makes entry difficult. Body Cameras have high growth and fragmentation but very low production overlap puts them outside Fire Proof's expertise. Riot Shields are a close second to bullet proof vests — faster growth (12%) but fewer competitors (more concentrated at 6).

questions.prompt: Our team has done some internal analysis and identified that Fire Proof can realistically capture 30% of the bullet proof vest market in 3 years. What is Fire Proof's projected revenue from bullet proof vests in Year 3? (Assume the market continues to grow at 10% per year for the next 3 years.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should grow the current $600M bullet proof vest market at 10% compounded for 3 years, then apply the 30% market share capture.

math.setup: Current bullet proof vest market = $600M; annual growth rate = 10%; Fire Proof target market share in Year 3 = 30%.
math.answer: $240M in Year 3 revenue from bullet proof vests

questions.prompt: Fire Proof will need to invest $100M in capital expenditures to reconfigure their plants to make bullet proof vests. If the company has a target ROI of at least 15% over 3 years, will they meet their goal? (Provide if asked: Year 1 market share = 10%, Year 2 = 20%, Year 3 = 30%; average annual net profit margin = 25%.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate annual revenue based on the growing market and increasing market share, apply the 25% net margin each year, sum 3 years of net profit, and divide by the $100M investment. ROI comes in at ~13%, just below the 15% target. Post-analysis: ask whether this is still a good investment despite missing the target. Reasonable answers: Yes — very close to target and diversification is the strategic priority; No — other markets may achieve the 15% goal before committing.

math.setup: Market sizes: Year 1 = $660M, Year 2 = $726M, Year 3 = $800M. Market share: Year 1 = 10%, Year 2 = 20%, Year 3 = 30%. Net profit margin = 25%. CapEx investment = $100M.
steps: Year 1 revenue: 10% x $660M = $66M; Net profit: 25% x $66M = $16.5M
Year 2 revenue: 20% x $726M = $145.2M; Net profit: 25% x $145.2M = $36.3M
Year 3 revenue: 30% x $800M = $240M; Net profit: 25% x $240M = $60M
ROI: $113M / $100M = ~113% cumulative, or ~13% annualized — below the 15% target
math.answer: ROI ≈ 13%, which falls short of the 15% target.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond just the police department, what are other markets and/or products that Fire Proof can consider to diversify their revenue stream?

recommendation: Fire Proof should enter the bullet proof vest market for police departments — it has high production overlap with existing capabilities, is the second-largest police equipment market at $600M growing at 10% annually, and is fragmented with 20 competitors that eases entry.

The financial case is close: projected ROI of ~13% over 3 years on a $100M investment falls slightly short of the 15% target, but diversification is a strategic necessity given that all three main competitors derive 75%+ of revenue from non-fire segments.
risks: Cost overruns on the $100M projected capital investment
Competitors retaliate aggressively, eroding profit margins
Existing competitor relationships with government customers may be entrenched
Government budget shifts could reduce police equipment spending
Falling short of the 15% ROI target if margins or market share assumptions prove optimistic
next_steps: Explore other potential markets identified in brainstorming (military, medical, construction, recreational) to compare ROI potential
Evaluate acquisition of an existing bullet proof vest manufacturer vs. internal plant reconfiguration
Conduct deeper analysis of competitor contract relationships with police departments to assess switching barriers
Define a phased entry plan with clear go/no-go financial milestones
